checks.note: JwtSecretService.addSecretToThread fetches via secretService.fetchSecret(JWT_VERSION, JWT_BUS_NAME) with no status parameter, consistent with the claim, but the actual query (SecretService.fetchSecret / findOneByVersionAndBusId) is not in this file, so whether EntityStatus is ignored cannot be confirmed here; the operational-procedure caveat is likewise outside this code.

SecretService.createSecret and fetchSecret call Map.of(..., VERSION, version, BUS_ID, busId) before validateVersion/validateBusId, and fetchLatestActiveSecretAsBytes wraps Map.of(..., BUS_ID, busId) in a HashMap before validateBusId; Map.of throws NPE on null values, so null inputs produce NPE instead of the BLANK_* SecException (StringUtils.isBlank would otherwise handle null). matches.note: R1 identifies the same defect: Jasypt password is reverse(busId+version) with constant values, so anyone with DB read access can decrypt the HS512 key and forge JWTs including admin.
